dedupe_keys.name: copper performance curve generator for building energy simulation

description: Copper is a Python tool that generates performance curves for heating and cooling equipment, such as chillers, for building energy simulation. It was developed at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory by Jérémy Lerond, Aowabin Rahman, Jian Zhang and Michael Rosenberg. Simulation programs describe how equipment efficiency varies with load and conditions through curves; Copper produces curves that capture typical part-load behaviour while matching a given set of design characteristics, including full-load and part-load efficiencies, so modellers can represent specific products or code-minimum equipment. Coverage: equipment types supported by the library, independent of location. Access: the package copper-bem on PyPI (version 0.3.0 uploaded 28 May 2026), with the 2023 version 0.1.7 archived on Zenodo; the source repository is maintained by PNNL. Licence: BSD 2-Clause; free. Caveats: generated curves are fitted to targets and typical shapes, not measured for each product. Simulation uses are more realistic HVAC plant models in building energy simulation for code compliance, design and retrofit analysis. Related records: EnergyPlus and OpenStudio.
inputs: Equipment design characteristics (full-load and part-load efficiencies, capacities)
